result.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
result.summary: LLM agents combine models with execution harnesses, so agentic benchmark performance reflects their joint behavior. We argue that harnesses should therefore be evaluated through their interactions with underlying models. We develop a framework combining five complementary measures: (i) Valid Completion Rate (VCR), how reliably agents finish normally and deliver evaluable results, irrespective of task correctness; (ii) Model-Harness Fit, how well a harness supports task achievement through valid completion for a given model; (iii) Cross-Model Fit, a harness's overall suitability across evaluated models; (iv) Interaction Residuals, pairing-specific execution strengths and weaknesses hidden by component-level summaries; and (v) Token Load, the token demands of agent execution, including failed attempts. We evaluate four general-purpose harnesses (OpenCode, Codex CLI, Pi CLI, and DeepAgents) with four core models, plus two fixed native model-harness systems, on six benchmarks covering context management, tool use, long-context planning, multimodal interaction, and artifact handoff. Including native references and stress conditions, 111 evaluation settings yield 52,168 trajectories. Harness rankings vary across models and benchmarks; task performance and valid completion can favor different pairings, and similar task scores can accompany distinct execution profiles. OpenCode ranks first in cross-model performance, while DeepSeek V4 Flash Preview maintains consistently high Mean VCR across harnesses on the shared four-benchmark panel. These findings support evaluating model-harness interactions, training transferable harness-use capabilities in models, and harness designs adapted to the model and task.

AI.brief_summary: 提出以模型与执行框架交互为中心的五项指标（有效完成率 VCR、模型-框架匹配、跨模型匹配、交互残差、token 负载），在六个基准上评测四种通用 agent 框架与四种模型的组合表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将整体表现拆为组件效应与配对交互残差、并把失败尝试的成本计入 token 负载的做法，可能可供核查用于区分 LVR 中基础模型能力与推理脚手架（如 THINK/LOOK/STOP）各自的贡献及真实开销。
